topic: Snowsight UX to mirage Console DATA VIEW and run PROFILE lens
summary: Snowsight made opaque server-side data ops legible after the fact - mirage's exact goal. Five surfaces: Query History, Query Profile (operator tree, Most Expensive Nodes, Profile Overview time split), results auto-profiling, the Databases catalog tree, a persistent role-warehouse selector. Mirage maps these onto a verified VfsOp spine; honesty boundary is sharp (no live SQL, client-side column profiles, fingerprint only on S3-like).

patternsToSteal.pattern: Query Profile operator tree: each node carries rows/bytes-scanned/percent-of-execution-time; arrows show rowset flow; the expensive node is found visually top-down.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Attributes cost to a SPECIFIC operation, not one aggregate latency, so the human points at the node that hurt; tree shape encodes causality (this scan fed that join).
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: PROFILE lens renders the Workspace-Run-Step-ToolCall-VfsOp waterfall as the operator tree. Node = VfsOp leaf from the replay actions array; per-node stats REAL: bytes, duration_ms, source, is_cache. Arrows = Step-to-ToolCall-to-VfsOps via stamped tool_call_id/run_id. Percent = op duration_ms over run sum. Tree and per-op bytes/source solid; latency-phase split (model vs cache vs fetch) is derived, label it.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Most Expensive Nodes pane: a flat ranked descending list of nodes at or above 1 percent of execution time, beside the tree, click-to-jump.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Triage entry point: turns staring at 40 operators into reading the top three rows. Ranked list, hard threshold.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: PROFILE lens Most Expensive Ops rail: VfsOps ranked by bytes (duration_ms toggle), row = op/path/mount_prefix/bytes/duration_ms/source. Click jumps the time-travel cursor (replay cursor, stateAt idx) to that op idx and rings it. Pure client derivation off the actions array, no new endpoint. The model-vs-data-mistake fast-path.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Profile Overview time split: total execution time into Processing, Local Disk IO, Remote Disk IO, Network, Initialization, as proportions.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Separates compute-bound from IO-bound from network-bound at a glance; a budget pie for one query.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: Run-level IO attribution strip from REAL signals: bytes by source (ram=cache/local vs disk=fetch), cache ratio = count is_cache over reads, bytes read vs written, per-mount bytes by effectClass (scratch, durable-internal, system-of-record, external-effect). Network/processing/init split is NOT emitted (Span tree is a demo); ship bytes-by-source plus cache-ratio plus bytes-by-mount solid, reserve a dimmed latency-phases slot. Served-from-cache DERIVED (is_cache==source ram), muted.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Query History as first-class objects: a columnar filterable list (SQL Text, Query ID, Status, User, Warehouse, Duration, Started) where each query opens to its own permalinkable detail with Details/Profile/Results tabs.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Makes the PAST the center of gravity; reviewing beats re-running. Durable, addressable, shareable, re-openable; filters turn a firehose into a worklist.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: This IS Home, the workspace RUN HISTORY. Each Run is the first-class object: durable, permalinkable, replayable (verified deterministic, persisted, survives restart). Columns from get_runs/get_steps/get_tool_calls/get_vfs_ops/list_sessions: run id, branch (TEST/LIVE), started, step count, op count, total bytes, write count, status. Filters: branch, wrote-anything, touched-mount, failed. Opening a run = Run view with three LENSES not tabs: PROFILE, TIME-TRAVEL, LINEAGE. Share=permalink; export=mirage-session.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Results auto-profiling: every result column gets fill/empty null counts, distinct for categoricals, a click-to-filter histogram for numeric/date columns, computed on returned rows.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Turns a dumb grid into an instant data-quality scanner: nulls, outliers, cardinality before any GROUP BY. Colocated, per column, interactive.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: DATA VIEW table-detail column-profile grid. Columns/types/nullable/PK from REAL schema.json; per-column profile (null percent, distinct, min/max, top values, sparkline) COMPUTED CLIENT-SIDE over data.jsonl (verified: stats.json table-level only, NO per-column distributions on disk). Label: computed client-side from sampled rows, no live SQL. Histogram for numeric/timestamptz (created_at, last_login, timestamp), top-values for categoricals (plan, status, event_type).

patternsToSteal.pattern: Databases object explorer: a database-to-schema-to-object catalog tree; selecting a table shows a Columns grid (name, type, nullable, PK), a Data Preview tab, and table stats (rows, bytes, created, last altered).
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: One persistent tree navigates ALL data with a consistent table-detail shape (schema/preview/stats); catalog and inspection in one surface.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: DATA VIEW catalog plus table-detail. Tree = 13 real mounts from _console_mounts_detail (prefix, resource, mode, effect_class) via vfsList (ls) and vfsFile (cat). The database mount is the Snowflake skin: a tables-t dir with schema.json/data.jsonl/stats.json renders a TableCard - Schema sub-tab (columns grid plus foreign_keys: users account_id to subscriptions, events user_id to users), Rows sub-tab (virtualized data.jsonl), Stats strip (users row_count 500, 105590 bytes, last_updated 2026-05-15). Non-table mounts (slack, s3, github) get a FILE-TREE skin with a vfsFile preview.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Persistent role-plus-warehouse context selector pinned in the header, scoping every query/result/catalog view, never hidden.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Ambient always-visible execution context kills the which-role/warehouse-ran-this confusion; single global state every surface inherits.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: The always-visible WORKSPACE context bar = persistent context (branch, TEST/LIVE), the role-plus-warehouse analog. Scopes Home, Run view, Data view identically; every list/op/catalog read is within this workspace and branch. Workspace-to-session persistence verified (history survives switches). Governance demoted: TEST/LIVE a quiet chip, promote stays Cmd-K-only.

mapsToMirage: Three altitudes: Workspace, Run/Trace, Action/VfsOp (per-pattern mirageUse has detail). The PROFILE-lens operator tree = the real Workspace-Run-Step-ToolCall-VfsOp waterfall; each node = the fully-stamped VfsOp leaf from GET /api/sessions/{id}/replay?cursor=&run_id= (op, path, source, bytes, duration_ms, mount_prefix, fingerprint, revision, is_cache, tool_call_id, run_id, timestamp). The bridge unique to mirage (no Snowsight analog): the LINEAGE Touched-by panel = get_vfs_ops filtered by mount_prefix+path, the exact data-to-trace join that reveals N runs/steps that read or wrote a path and cursor-jumps back into the waterfall. Verified source anchors: _replay_action/_fold_replay_state/session_replay (server.py 1691-1784); _console_mounts_detail (server.py ~2323); vfs_list/vfs_file (server.py 2000-2024); store get_runs/get_steps/get_tool_calls/get_vfs_ops/list_sessions (packages/store/arcadia_store/sql_store.py 116-176); schema.json/data.jsonl/stats.json under packages/eval/scenarios/northhill_corp/fixture/disk/database/tables/{users,invoices,subscriptions,events}; catalog-proxy NotImplementedError (packages/catalog-proxy/catalog_proxy/proxy.py 28,39 + adapters/iceberg.py, adapters/mcp.py).
concreteLayout: DATA VIEW = three columns under the persistent Workspace context bar (branch, TEST/LIVE); dark, dense, keyboard-first; one keystroke from Home. LEFT, CATALOG TREE (~300px): mount list from _console_mounts_detail - each row prefix (root, slack, sheets, gdocs, tickets, github, pagerduty, datadog, finance, customers, compliance, database, s3), resource, ro/rw chip, effect-class dot with reversibility tooltip, browsed-as file-tree-or-table subtitle, derived touched-by-N-runs rollup; lazy-expand via vfsList; database/tables-t flag the table skin. CENTER, type-aware. TABLE skin: header = table name + Stats strip from stats.json (row_count 500, 105590 bytes, last_updated 2026-05-15); a DISABLED query bar (tooltip: live query.json/catalog-proxy, schema designed, NotImplementedError); sub-tabs Schema (columns grid from schema.json + foreign_keys row) and Data (virtualized data.jsonl grid, each header carrying its mini column-profile + click-to-filter); muted note: derived from files, column profile computed client-side, no live SQL. FILE-TREE skin (slack, s3, github): breadcrumb + vfsFile preview + honesty strip (preview only, text decode, no binary/truncation). RIGHT (~400px), two stacked panels. COLUMN PROFILE for the selected column: null-percent fill/empty bar, distinct, min/max, top-values (categoricals) or histogram (numeric/timestamptz), header: computed client-side from N sampled rows. LINEAGE Touched-by: get_vfs_ops by mount_prefix+path; header M actions touched, R read / W write; rows op/idx/bytes/source/duration_ms + run-or-step deep-link, tagged inferred where op-to-step is pre-stamp, + written/read sparkline; click jumps the cursor into that run waterfall (stateAt idx) and rings the op; below, a ReservedMetadataStrip (fingerprint/revision/consistency = dash on disk mounts, S3-only via ETag). RUN PROFILE lens (sibling, same shell): LEFT operator tree (Step-ToolCall-VfsOp waterfall reusing RunTracePanel/StepCard/ToolCallRow/ReasoningBlock); CENTER-TOP Most Expensive Ops rail (VfsOps by bytes/duration_ms, click-to-cursor); CENTER selected VfsOp leaf detail + the INTENT-plus-COMMAND card (self-reported intent labeled, then command, then this op observed effect); RIGHT IO-attribution strip (bytes-by-source, cache-ratio, bytes-by-mount by effectClass) + dimmed latency-phases reserved slot. Top context bar = role-plus-warehouse analog (Workspace dropdown, branch chip, Cmd-K, Home/Run/DATA switch).
pitfalls: NO LIVE SQL: catalog-proxy proxy.py and query.json raise NotImplementedError (proxy.py 28,39; adapters iceberg.py, mcp.py). Query bar MUST be present-but-disabled, tooltip live query.json/catalog-proxy schema designed NotImplementedError. Do not let the worksheet metaphor imply typing SQL.

Per-column distributions are NOT on disk: stats.json is table-level only (row_count, size_bytes, last_updated; verified users/invoices/subscriptions/events). Histograms, null percent, distinct, min/max, top-values must be COMPUTED CLIENT-SIDE from data.jsonl and labeled so - not authoritative engine statistics.

fingerprint/revision/consistency real only on S3-like sources. The 13 mounts are fake resources subclassing DiskResource browsed via ls -la and cat, which drops these. Render a dash on disk mounts (S3-only via ETag), solid only where the source provides them. Never fabricate.

Profile Overview phase split (Processing, Local/Remote Disk IO, Network, Initialization) is NOT emitted; Span tree is a demo, true cache hits emit no OpRecord. Ship bytes-by-source + cache-ratio + bytes-by-mount solid; latency-phase is a dimmed not-yet-emitted slot. Served-from-cache DERIVED (is_cache==source ram), muted.

Intent is self-reported, not hosted cognition: the why comes from AG-UI THINKING (partial), so the intent-not-equal-effect flag compares stated vs observed only. Label intent muted/self-reported; design the card to upgrade when a model gateway lands.

op-to-step is now stamped (tool_call_id/run_id on the leaf), but pre-stamp ops and timestamp-merge ordering still carry the inferred chip until Phase 0 lands. Only the VfsOp leaf, the exact diff, the mount_prefix+path Touched-by join, and the stateAt idx fold are solid ground truth; keep tiers strict.

Lineage is a JOIN, not a graph: Touched-by is buildable (get_vfs_ops by mount_prefix+path), but the OpenLineage provenance graph is NotImplementedError. Do not draw FK edges between tables as observed dataflow; FK arrows are static schema from schema.json. Reserve the graph as dimmed.

topic: Databricks UX deep-dive → mirage LINEAGE lens (the touched-by join) + run-spine drill-in
summary: Databricks gives mirage three load-bearing UX patterns, each verified against docs.databricks.com. (1) Unity Catalog LINEAGE: every table has a Lineage tab with an interactive bidirectional graph (one hop by default, "+" to expand) PLUS a filterable Lineage details panel that lists the actual notebooks/jobs/pipelines/queries/dashboards that read or wrote it — the data↔compute bridge, backed by a system table with one record per read/write event. This maps almost 1:1 onto mirage's touched-by join, with one honest difference: mirage's join is op-level and session/run-scoped, not a metastore-wide provenance graph. (2) Jobs & Runs: runs are durable, listable, 60-day-retained objects; the Runs tab has matrix + list views (status/duration/trigger/start-time columns), and you drill job→run→task→stage/logs via a task DAG — this is mirage's run-spine drill-in (Run → Step(intent) → ToolCall(command) → VfsOp leaf). (3) Persistent workspace + Recents in the left sidebar (catalog/workflows/compute as connected categories) maps to mirage's workspace context bar + run-history Home. The decisive grounding fact: mirage's real data layer (`/api/sessions/{id}/replay`) returns an ordered `actions[]` of `ReplayAction` leaves, each carrying `op·path·source·bytes·duration_ms·mount_prefix·fingerprint·revision·is_cache·tool_call_id·run_id` — exactly the columns Unity Catalog's lineage system table carries per event. But `get_vfs_ops(session_id, run_id)` filters ONLY by session+run; there is no `/api/lineage` or `/api/touched-by` endpoint and no path/mount filter, so the bidirectional touched-by join must be computed client-side over one session/run's `actions[]`. And `emit_read`/`emit_write` in `packages/lineage/lineage_emitter/emitter.py` both `raise NotImplementedError` (OpenLineage is a schema only), CatalogProxy/Iceberg/MCP adapters + `query.json` are all NotImplementedError — so mirage Lineage today is read/write pairs, NOT a full provenance graph or column-level lineage. The Databricks graph is the aspirational shape to gesture at (dimmed), while the honest shippable surface is the op-level touched-by list with a 2-hop neighborhood (path ↔ run/step ↔ sibling paths in the same run).

patternsToSteal.pattern: Lineage as a TAB on the data object, not a separate app. In Unity Catalog the Lineage tab lives on the table next to Overview/Sample Data/Details, so lineage is always answered in the data object's own context ('who touched THIS').
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Anchors the abstract relationship to the concrete thing the user is staring at; you never lose the subject. Lineage is a property of the object, discovered in place.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: In mirage's Data view, every path/file gets a 'LINEAGE — touched by N runs/steps' panel (brief Directive 2 names this explicitly). Backed by client-side filter of `actions[]` where `mount_prefix+path` matches the selected node. Solid (ground truth: the VfsOp leaf join).

patternsToSteal.pattern: Bidirectional graph with progressive expansion — one hop shown by default, click the '+' on a node to pull the next upstream/downstream layer; click an EDGE to open a 'Lineage details' panel naming the relationship's source+target.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Prevents the hairball. Lineage graphs explode combinatorially; defaulting to one hop + explicit expansion keeps cognitive load bounded and makes each expansion a deliberate question.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: mirage's honest analog is a 2-hop neighborhood, NOT a recursive graph: data path → (hop 1) the runs/steps that touched it → (hop 2) the OTHER paths those same runs/steps touched (via shared run_id/tool_call_id in `actions[]`). Render as an expandable list/mini-graph, default collapsed at hop 1. Label deeper provenance dimmed/'not yet' (no transitive table→table edges exist).

patternsToSteal.pattern: Filter lineage by ASSET TYPE (Notebooks / Jobs / Pipelines / Queries / Dashboards) inside the details panel.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Lets one panel answer many questions (impact analysis vs root-cause) by slicing the same edge set by consumer/producer kind.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: mirage's available facets are real and narrower: filter touched-by rows by OP TYPE (read vs write — the read/write distinction IS the lineage primitive), by SOURCE (s3/disk/ram-cache), and by RUN. 'is_cache' (derived from source=='ram') gets a muted facet. No notebook/job/pipeline taxonomy exists — don't fake those buckets.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Impact analysis vs root-cause as the two named user journeys: downstream = 'what breaks if I change this', upstream = 'where did this bad value come from'.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Gives the bidirectional graph a job-to-be-done in each direction, so the two arrows aren't symmetric decoration.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: mirage reframes to the brief's core question 'model mistake vs data mistake?': from a DATA path → which runs/steps consumed it (was the input stale? check fingerprint/revision); from a VfsOp/step → which data object produced the bytes the agent acted on. Both directions are the same `actions[]` join read two ways.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Job lineage reachable FROM the run, not only from the table — Databricks puts an 'upstream/downstream tables' link in the Job details panel, closing the compute→data loop from the run side.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Makes the bridge truly bidirectional in the UI: you can start from either pane (catalog or workflows) and cross to the other.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: Directly the run-side of mirage's bridge: on a Run/Step, a 'Data touched' affordance lists the distinct mount_prefix+paths in that run's `actions[]`, each linking into the Data view (and from the VfsOp leaf, deep-link straight to that path's Data view + back to this op). This is the VfsOp→data-object direction the task asks for.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Runs as durable, listable, permalinkable objects with a Runs tab (matrix + list), 60-day retention, columns = status/duration/trigger/start-time, and per-run drill-in.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Treating each execution as a first-class durable noun (not an ephemeral log) is what makes review the center of gravity — you can come back to a run hours later and re-interrogate it.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: Exactly mirage's settled object model (Run/Trace = THE noun: durable, listable, permalinkable, replayable). Home = run-history (Snowflake query-history style). Backed by `listSessions`/`get_runs`; replay is deterministic and survives restart. Solid.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Task-DAG drill-in: job→run→task→Spark-stage→executor-logs, with a Graph view (click a node for task details: source code, cluster, metrics) and a Timeline view (click a query statement → its query profile).
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Each level of the hierarchy answers a different altitude of 'what happened', and the lowest level is the literal ground-truth execution unit.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: mirage's run-spine is the analog DAG: Run → Step(intent, self-reported via AG-UI THINKING) → ToolCall(command) → VfsOp(observed leaf). The brief's INTENT+COMMAND card IS the task node; the VfsOp leaf (bytes·source·cache·fingerprint·exit) is mirage's 'Spark stage' — the granular ground truth. Already built: RunTracePanel/StepCard/ToolCallRow/ReasoningBlock.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Persistent workspace + Recents in a left sidebar; catalog / workflows / compute as connected, switchable categories sharing one context.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Your work survives and the panes are connected — you cross from a notebook to the table it reads to the job that ran it without losing your place.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: mirage's always-visible workspace context bar (branch · TEST/LIVE, like role+warehouse) + Home run-history + Cmd-K + Recents. Honesty caveat: Databricks Recents is browser-storage-backed, mirage's workspace→session persistence is server-side (Phase-0 fix: history survives switches), so mirage is actually stronger here — say so.

mapsToMirage:
The Databricks lineage system-table record (one row per read/write event, carrying entity + path) is field-for-field the mirage `ReplayAction` leaf returned by `GET /api/sessions/{id}/replay?cursor=&run_id=`: `{idx, op, path, source, bytes, duration_ms, mount_prefix, fingerprint, revision, is_cache, tool_call_id, run_id, timestamp}` (frontends/platform/src/types/replay.ts; emitted by `_replay_action` at frontends/platform/server.py:1691). So mirage's LINEAGE lens = the 'touched-by' JOIN computed over `actions[]`, in BOTH directions:

• DATA → RUNS (Data view): user selects a path P. Filter `actions[]` where `mount_prefix+path == P` (the brief's exact 'mount_prefix+path → trace bridge'). Group by `run_id` → 'touched by N runs', and within a run by `tool_call_id` → the exact step/command. Each row = {op (read/write), source, bytes, is_cache, fingerprint, revision} → deep-link to that Run/Step. This is Workspace>Data>path → its touched-by list.

• VfsOp → DATA (Run view): user is on a VfsOp leaf (cursor_op from the replay fold, or a StepCard's op). Its `mount_prefix+path` IS the data object — one click opens Workspace>Data>that-path, and the reverse touched-by list lights up showing every run that touched it. The `state.cursor_op` and `state.diff` from `_fold_replay_state` (server.py:1709) already hand you the selected op + its read/write diff.

• 2-HOP NEIGHBORHOOD (the honest 'graph'): from path P, hop-1 = runs/steps that touched P; hop-2 = the OTHER distinct paths those same runs touched (group P's runs' `actions[]` by path). This is read↔write co-occurrence within a run — the closest honest thing to upstream/downstream. It is NOT transitive provenance.

Run-spine drill-in maps to Databricks job→run→task→stage: Workspace(branch·TEST/LIVE) → Run (durable, from `get_runs`/`listSessions`) → Step(intent, AG-UI THINKING, self-reported) → ToolCall(command) → VfsOp(leaf = mirage's 'Spark stage'). The replay `cursor`/`stateAt(idx)` fold gives Redux-style scrub down the spine.

CRITICAL DATA CONSTRAINT (drives every layout decision): `get_vfs_ops(session_id, run_id)` (packages/store/arcadia_store/sql_store.py:145) filters ONLY by session+run — there is NO path/mount filter and NO `/api/lineage` or `/api/touched-by` route in server.py. So the touched-by join is CLIENT-SIDE over one session/run's `actions[]`, and is scoped to the current workspace's sessions, NOT a metastore-wide cross-workspace graph. 'Touched by N runs' means N runs you've loaded in this workspace, not all-history. Frontend already has the parts (sessionRunStore, consoleStore, correlateEvents.ts which buckets events→steps by timestamp window).
concreteLayout:
LINEAGE is a LENS that renders the SAME touched-by join in two homes. Dark, dense, keyboard-first.

═══ A. THE LINEAGE PANEL inside the DATA VIEW (data → runs direction) ═══
Workspace > Data > [path tree | path detail]. The path-detail right column stacks: Preview → Schema/Columns grid → Metadata → and at the bottom a pinned "LINEAGE — Touched by" card:

┌ LINEAGE · /s3/dashboards/checkout.json ─────────────────────[graph ⤢]┐
│ Touched by 3 runs · 5 ops          [● read 4] [● write 1] [src: s3] │  ← op-type + source facets (real)
│ ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│
│ ▸ run_a1f… "correlate the deploy"        2 ops   ◀read ◀read        │  ← group by run_id; each row deep-links to Run view
│   └ tool_call_3c…  cat …/checkout.json   read · s3 · 12.4KB · fp:a91│     leaf line = the VfsOp (solid)
│   └ tool_call_3c…  cat …/checkout.json   read · ram-cache ⓘ         │     is_cache muted (derived: source==ram)
│ ▸ run_b27… "patch the dashboard"         1 op    ▶write             │
│   └ tool_call_9e…  write …/checkout.json write · +840B · rev:R7     │     fingerprint/rev solid only on s3-like
│ ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│
│ Co-touched in these runs (hop-2):  /s3/metrics/latency.json  ·  …   │  ← honest 2-hop neighborhood
│ ⓘ Op-level lineage from observed VfsOps in THIS workspace's runs.    │  ← honesty footer
│   Not a transitive provenance graph. [graph ⤢] = preview, dimmed.   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
[graph ⤢] opens a DIMMED mini-graph: center node = path; left = runs that read; right = runs that wrote; hop-2 paths as faint satellites. Labeled "preview · op-level, not provenance".

═══ B. THE LINEAGE AFFORDANCE inside the RUN VIEW (VfsOp → data direction) ═══
Run view = INTENT+COMMAND cards down the spine (existing RunTracePanel/StepCard). On each VfsOp leaf row and in the right-hand inspector when an op is selected:

  StepCard ▸ "read the live checkout dashboard to correlate the deploy"   ⚠INTENT≠EFFECT?
    └ ToolCall  cat /s3/dashboards/checkout.json
        └ VfsOp  read · s3 · 12.4KB · fp:a91 · exit 0     [↗ Data]  [touched-by 3]
                                                            ▲          ▲
                              deep-link to Data view of    │          │ count = #runs touching this path
                              this exact path ─────────────┘          │ (client join); click → reverse list

Right inspector (when a VfsOp is selected, fed by replay `state.cursor_op`+`state.diff`):
  ┌ OP /s3/dashboards/checkout.json ───────────┐
  │ read · s3 · 12.4KB · dur 41ms              │  solid
  │ fingerprint a91… · revision R7             │  solid (s3-like only)
  │ is_cache: no  ⓘ derived (source≠ram)       │  muted
  │ ── Data object ──────── [open in Data ↗] ──│  ← VfsOp→data bridge
  │ ── Touched by (this workspace) ────────────│  ← reverse join, same component as panel A
  │   ▸ this run (current) · ▸ run_b27 write   │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────┘

═══ C. HOW IT SITS IN THE SHELL (connected panes, Databricks-style) ═══
Left sidebar categories (always-visible context bar on top: workspace · branch · TEST/LIVE):
  Home(run history) · Runs · Data(catalog) · Compare · Investigation · [Cmd-K]
The Lineage lens is NOT its own nav item — it is the cross-link that makes Data ⇄ Runs bidirectional, exactly like Databricks puts the lineage tab on the table AND the upstream/downstream-tables link on the job. Cmd-K jumps path↔run. Selecting an op anywhere updates a shared selection so the reverse panel stays in sync (use existing consoleStore/sessionRunStore pattern).
pitfalls: HONESTY — op-level, NOT provenance: `emit_read`/`emit_write` in packages/lineage/lineage_emitter/emitter.py:30,51 both `raise NotImplementedError`; OpenLineage is only a Pydantic schema (openlineage.py). There is NO derived table→table provenance, NO transitive upstream/downstream chain. mirage 'lineage' = read/write pairs (which run touched which path). Do NOT draw a recursive Databricks-style provenance graph as if it's real — the [graph ⤢] view must be visually dimmed and labeled 'op-level, not provenance / preview'.

NO column-level lineage. Databricks shows which upstream COLUMNS feed a column (e.g. 'revenue'). mirage has nothing of the kind — column profiles in the Data grid are client-side-computed from data.jsonl, and there is zero column→column derivation. Never render column lineage edges.

The touched-by join is CLIENT-SIDE and SESSION/RUN-SCOPED, not metastore-wide. `get_vfs_ops(session_id, run_id)` (sql_store.py:145) filters only by session+run; there is no `/api/lineage`/`/api/touched-by` route and no path/mount filter on the server. 'Touched by N runs' must say 'in this workspace's loaded runs', not imply an all-history cross-workspace index. The cross-run join requires fetching each run's `actions[]` and unioning client-side.

NO notebook/job/pipeline/dashboard asset taxonomy. Databricks filters lineage by those 5 asset types; mirage has none of them. The only honest facets are op-type (read/write), source (s3/disk/ram), and run_id. Do not invent 'jobs'/'pipelines' filter chips.

INTENT is self-reported, not ground truth. The INTENT+COMMAND card's 'why' comes from AG-UI THINKING (partial, self-reported) because mirage does not host the cognition plane — so the INTENT≠EFFECT flag is a heuristic, not a verdict. Label intent muted; design the card to upgrade when a model gateway lands. (Carries into lineage because lineage rows surface the intent string.)

`is_cache` is DERIVED (`source == 'ram'`, server.py:1702) — render it muted, never as a first-class measured field. Same for any op→step pre-stamp / timestamp-merge correlation (correlateEvents.ts buckets events into steps by timestamp window, which is inferred, not stamped).

fingerprint/revision are REAL only on S3-like sources; on Fake*Resource(DiskResource) demo tables they are null. The touched-by leaf must show fingerprint/revision solid only when present and omit (not zero-fill) otherwise, or it implies content-addressing that the disk sources don't have.

NO live SQL / query.json: CatalogProxy + Iceberg/Snowflake/MCP adapters and the query.json handler all `raise NotImplementedError` (packages/catalog-proxy, packages/workspace-vfs). The Data view's query bar must be disabled with a 'derived from files' note; lineage cannot show 'queries' as a consumer type.

Don't over-promise the 2-hop neighborhood as 'upstream/downstream'. Hop-2 (co-touched paths in the same run) is read↔write CO-OCCURRENCE, not directional data flow — a write in the same run as a read does not prove the write derived from the read. Label it 'co-touched in these runs', not 'downstream of'.

topic: Redux DevTools deep-dive (TIME-TRAVEL lens on /replay) + the INTENT+COMMAND card (directive 1), grounded in Arcadia's real /replay endpoint, AG-UI trace, and the stamped VfsOp correlation chain
summary: The v3 brief converges two jobs onto substrate that already exists and is tested. (A) Redux DevTools' core loop is state=fold(actions): an action list on the left, an inspector with Action/State/Diff/Trace tabs, a bottom transport (jump/skip/slider/play), per-action diff, and import/export of a session. This maps almost 1:1 onto the real GET /api/sessions/{id}/replay endpoint (server.py L1756): actions[] is the exact ordered VfsOp leaf list from get_vfs_ops (persisted, survives restart), and state=stateAt(cursor) is a literal left-fold _fold_replay_state over actions[:cursor+1] (L1709) producing overlay (last-write-wins by path), reads_so_far (read-path set), cursor_op (=actions[cursor]), and diff (the per-action delta: write→added_bytes, read→source/cache/fingerprint/revision). What is EXACT: the action ordering, action idx==OpRecord position, the fold, the write-overlay, the per-VfsOp diff. What is DERIVED: is_cache (computed source=="ram" at L1702), the default cursor (clamped to total-1), reads_so_far has no byte/fingerprint detail (only path set sorted), and skip-action is a client re-fold what-if, not a re-drive. (B) The INTENT+COMMAND card is the new run-inspection grain: operative-intent + command + observed-effect. The full correlation chain it needs is already stamped at emission (server.py L1414-1426 puts tool_call_id+step_id+run_id on every vfs_op) and persisted relationally (models.py: vfs_ops.tool_call_id→tool_calls.step_id→steps.run_id, with steps.reasoning holding the verbatim intent and tool_calls.args/result/exit_code holding command+stdout). The honesty boundary is sharp and code-provable: intent is SELF-REPORTED, because the system prompt only says the agent "may show your reasoning wrapped in <thinking>" (L820-822), parsed by _route_think (L1180) into AG-UI THINKING events, or pulled from reasoning_content deltas (L1147) when a reasoning gateway exposes them — never observed cognition. So the card must degrade honestly when reasoning is absent and label intent as self-reported, upgrading cleanly when a hosted cognition plane lands. One critical exact-vs-derived nuance for BOTH jobs: the live useAgentStream reducer's VfsOp type drops tool_call_id/fingerprint/revision (agui.ts L160-168, reducer L322-328), so the live path is lossy — the persisted /replay path is the authoritative source for correlation, diff, and the intent≠effect flag.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Redux: state = fold over actions, with one global cursor. The store IS the workspace/run; actions ARE the I/O; jumping the cursor re-derives state purely. The action list and the inspector are two views of the same cursor.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: It is a debugger mental model, not a dashboard. There is exactly one source of truth (the action log) and everything else is a pure projection at idx — so it is deterministic, permalinkable (?cursor=idx), and impossible to desync. Engineers already trust it.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: EXACT on /replay: actions[] = the persisted VfsOp leaf list (server.py _replay_action L1691, fields op/path/source/bytes/duration_ms/mount_prefix/fingerprint/revision/is_cache/tool_call_id/run_id/timestamp). stateAt(idx) = _fold_replay_state over actions[:cursor+1] (L1709). The cursor is `cursor` in ReplayResponse; jump = re-request or re-fold at a new idx. No client-side reducer needed for VfsOp state — the server already folds it.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Redux inspector tabs over the SELECTED action: Action (raw dispatched object) / State (full tree after it) / Diff (what THIS action changed) / Trace (where it was dispatched from — the call stack/causality).
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: One selection, four altitudes. Diff answers 'what did this do', State answers 'what is true now', Action answers 'what exactly was this', Trace answers 'why did this fire'. You never lose the selected atom while changing depth.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: Map each tab to real fields of cursor_op + state: ACTION tab = the raw ReplayAction object (all 12 fields, solid). STATE tab = state.overlay + state.reads_so_far + state.reads_count folded to idx (solid; render via existing OverlayDiff renderer, OverlayDiff.tsx). DIFF tab = state.diff (EXACT for a VfsOp: write→{kind,path,added_bytes,mount_prefix}; read→{kind,path,source,is_cache,fingerprint,revision}). TRACE tab = the 'dispatched from' causality = the stamped tool_call_id→step→run join (models.py chain): this action was dispatched by tool_call tc-… (command = tool_calls.args) inside step step-… whose reasoning IS the intent. This is the bridge between the two jobs.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Redux 'dispatched from' / action trace: every action carries the stack of WHO dispatched it, so you can click an action and jump to the code/thunk that fired it.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Causality is the hardest thing to reconstruct after the fact. Pre-stamping the dispatch origin turns 'why did this happen' from archaeology into a single click.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: EXACT and already emitted: every VfsOp is stamped with tool_call_id+step_id+run_id at emission (server.py L1424-1426). So the action's 'dispatched from' is: command = tool_calls.args (the cat/ls/jq string), intent = steps.reasoning, run = runs.run_id. This is the literal seam where the Trace tab becomes the INTENT+COMMAND card. CAVEAT: stamping is solid in the persisted path only; the live reducer drops it (agui.ts VfsOp has no tool_call_id) — so derive causality from /replay, not from useAgentStream.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Redux transport: a draggable slider/playhead over the action stream + play/pause + step-back/step-forward + jump-to-start/end + a skip toggle per action (action stays in the log but is excluded from the fold).
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Scrubbing makes the fold tangible — you SEE state grow as the playhead sweeps. Skip is a what-if: 'did the later write actually depend on this read?' without re-running anything.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: JUMP/SLIDER = set cursor=idx, re-fold (deterministic; server clamps cursor to total-1 at L1775, so the playhead range is [0, total-1]). PLAY = animate cursor over actions[].timestamp (real wall-clock spacing). SKIP = client-side re-fold of actions minus the skipped idx under a 'hypothetical: action N skipped' banner — HONEST because the fold is pure; enabled for overlay/reads (recomputable), and labeled as a state-reconstruction what-if, NOT a re-drive (DESIGN.md L91). The mini-map density = bytes or op-count per action.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Redux import/export: serialize the whole session (action log + computed state) to a file a teammate re-imports to scrub offline — the bug repro becomes a shareable artifact.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: Turns a live debugging session into a portable, deterministic artifact. The receiver replays the exact same actions and gets the exact same state — no environment needed.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: Export = generalize the verified TrajectoryPage.exportJson (TrajectoryPage.tsx L104, Blob+download) to a .mirage-session.json = the full /replay actions[] + the getSessionTrace AG-UI events (for reasoning/messages/tool calls) + the mount manifest. Import re-hydrates: AG-UI via replayAguiEvents (aguiEventReducer.ts L341), VfsOp state via the same _fold_replay_state logic ported client-side. HONEST: backing-FS reconstruction is deferred (StatePage.tsx L262 already says so) — label the imported session 'scrub limited to overlay/reads/run; backing pinned at stand-up'.

patternsToSteal.pattern: INTENT+COMMAND card (directive 1): the primary run-inspection unit is a trio — operative intent (why) paired with the command it produced paired with that command's observed effect — with verbatim reasoning + full stdout one click away (progressive disclosure), and an INTENT≠EFFECT flag.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: It makes each action self-explaining and powers the core question 'model mistake vs data mistake?'. When the stated intent ('read the LIVE checkout dashboard') and the observed effect ('read /s3/dashboards/checkout_2023.json, served from cache') disagree, the flag surfaces a model error; when they agree but the data is wrong, it is a data error.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: Every field is real: INTENT = steps.reasoning (folded from THINKING). COMMAND = tool_calls.args + tool_name (the exec string). EFFECT = the VfsOp leaf from /replay (op·path·source·bytes·is_cache·fingerprint·revision) + tool_calls.exit_code. The trio is joined by the stamped tool_call_id (models.py). Grain is collapsible Step(intent)→[ToolCall(command)→VfsOps] because one agent iteration emits THINKING then multiple exec_lines (server.py L1389-1447) — exactly StepCard→ToolCallRow→effect rows, which already exist (StepCard.tsx). INTENT≠EFFECT is computed: does the path/source/cache in the reasoning text match the observed VfsOp? (heuristic on the demo: e.g. reasoning says 'live'/'latest' but effect is is_cache=true, or names a different path than the one read).

patternsToSteal.pattern: Honest degradation + clean upgrade for self-reported signals: label a signal's provenance inline (solid = observed, muted = self-reported/derived) and reserve the upgraded slot so the UI doesn't change shape when ground truth arrives.
patternsToSteal.whyItWorks: It keeps trust intact — the user always knows whether intent is the model's own narration or observed cognition — and it means shipping today doesn't paint you into a corner when a cognition plane lands.
patternsToSteal.mirageUse: Intent is self-reported TODAY: system prompt only says agent 'may show your reasoning wrapped in <thinking>' (server.py L820-822), parsed by _route_think (L1180) or reasoning_content deltas (L1147) — both are AG-UI THINKING, never observed. So the intent row carries a muted 'self-reported · AG-UI THINKING' chip; when steps.reasoning is empty, show 'no stated intent for this step' (not a fabrication). UPGRADE slot: when a hosted gateway emits observed cognition, the SAME row flips to a solid 'observed intent' chip — no layout change. EFFECT and COMMAND are always solid (they are observed I/O).

mapsToMirage: OBJECT MODEL: Workspace (context bar) > Run (the noun, runs table) > Action/VfsOp (the atom, vfs_ops table). The two jobs sit on the Run-view's two lenses: TIME-TRAVEL and the INTENT+COMMAND grain. EXACT mappings from the real /replay endpoint (server.py L1756, types/replay.ts ReplayResponse): action list ← actions[] (ordered VfsOps from get_vfs_ops, persisted); State tab ← state.overlay (last-write-wins dict, _fold L1712-1721) + state.reads_so_far (sorted read-path set, L1722-1728) + state.reads_count; Diff tab ← state.diff (EXACT per-action: write→added_bytes/mount_prefix, read→source/is_cache/fingerprint/revision, L1730-1746); Action tab ← cursor_op (=actions[cursor], all 12 fields); cursor/slider ← `cursor` int, range [0,total-1] (clamped L1775); jump ← re-request with ?cursor=idx; import/export ← actions[]+getSessionTrace events, exportJson basis at TrajectoryPage.tsx L104. The 'dispatched from' Trace tab ← the stamped correlation chain: ReplayAction.tool_call_id → tool_calls (args=command, result/exit_code=stdout) → tool_calls.step_id → steps (reasoning=intent) → steps.run_id → runs. This same chain IS the INTENT+COMMAND card: INTENT=steps.reasoning (self-reported via THINKING fold, aguiEventReducer.ts L160-190), COMMAND=tool_calls.args (=TOOL_CALL_ARGS.delta, the exec string), EFFECT=the VfsOp leaf + exit_code. getSessionTrace (client.ts L244) supplies reasoning/messages/tool calls for the verbatim-reasoning and full-stdout progressive-disclosure layers. DERIVED/MUTED (label, don't fake): is_cache=source=='ram' (server.py L1702); reads_so_far carries no per-read bytes/fingerprint (only the path set); op→step attribution is exact ONLY in /replay (live reducer drops tool_call_id, agui.ts L160-168 + reducer L322-328); skip-action is a pure client re-fold what-if; intent provenance is self-reported (system prompt 'may show', L820). NOT-YET (dimmed): observed cognition/hosted intent, latency-phase breakdown, lineage graph, live SQL.
concreteLayout:
RUN VIEW = one organism, three regions over a single shared cursor (permalink ?cursor=idx&lens=…).

REGION 1 — LEFT RAIL (380px): the ACTION LIST. Two grouping modes (Flat ⇄ By-Step), toggle pinned at top. Flat = virtualized reverse-or-forward list of ReplayAction rows: [idx gutter] [op chip: read/write/append] [path, truncated] [source dot] [±bytes] [effect-class dot for writes] [muted 'cache' chip when is_cache]. By-Step = the existing StepCard tree (StepCard.tsx): step header (name, duration, n calls, n VFS, bytes) → expands to the INTENT+COMMAND cards. Rows/segments PAST the cursor render at ~45% opacity ('not yet executed' left border).

REGION 2 — CENTER INSPECTOR: a lens tab strip over the selected action — ACTION · STATE · DIFF · TRACE.
  • DIFF (default): top = a compact INTENT+COMMAND card for cursor_op's owning step (see below); below = the git-style hunk via the existing OverlayDiff renderer (op icon · path · ±bytes · CaptureBadge · effect-class dot) for writes, or a read-preview card (source · is_cache · fingerprint/revision, with '—, S3-only' for disk sources) for reads. Both come straight from state.diff.
  • STATE: the folded tree at idx — Overlay node (state.overlay, last-write-wins) · Reads-so-far node (state.reads_so_far, with a muted 'paths only — no per-read bytes' note) · Mounts node (prefix/mode/effect_class) · a reserved-dimmed 'state (snapshot)' stub.
  • ACTION: the raw ReplayAction JSON (all 12 fields, solid).
  • TRACE ('dispatched from'): the causality crumb — run-… › step-… › tool_call tc-… › THIS op — each segment clickable; this tab hosts the FULL INTENT+COMMAND card.

THE INTENT+COMMAND CARD (the directive-1 unit, used in both By-Step rail and the Trace tab):
  ┌─ Step N · [status dot] step-name · 1.2s · 2 cmds ──────────────────┐
  │ INTENT  [muted chip: 'self-reported · THINKING']                   │  ← steps.reasoning, 2-line clamp; '▸ verbatim' expands full reasoning (getSessionTrace)
  │   "read the live checkout dashboard to correlate the deploy"        │
  │   ── if empty: 'No stated intent for this step' (muted italic) ──    │
  ├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ ▾ COMMAND  $ cat /s3/dashboards/checkout.json      exit 0  · 6ms     │  ← tool_calls.args + exit_code; '▸ full stdout' expands tool_calls.result
  │     └─ EFFECT  read · /s3/dashboards/checkout_2023.json              │  ← the VfsOp leaf; click → cursor jumps to that action's Diff
  │              s3 · 4.2 KB · rev v3 · etag-9a1f · [cache]              │
  │     [⚑ INTENT≠EFFECT  'live' intent vs cached read of a 2023 path]   │  ← solid amber flag when stated intent disagrees with observed op
  │ ▸ COMMAND  $ jq '.errors' …                          exit 0 · 2ms    │  ← second command in the same step (collapsible, proves Step→[cmds] grain)
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
  Card grain = Step(intent) → [ToolCall(command) → VfsOps]; commands collapse independently. Intent is the step-level row (one per step); command+effect repeat per tool call.

REGION 3 — BOTTOM TRANSPORT BAR (36px, full width): density mini-map of actions[] (bar height = bytes) with a draggable playhead; ⏮ step-back · ▶/⏸ play · step-fwd ⏭ · jump-to-end; 1×/2×/4× speed; right side 'cursor #K of M · idx N · 12:04:07.214' (from cursor_op.timestamp). A 'hypothetical: action N skipped — revert' banner spans the inspector when a skip is active. Right of the bar: Export session button (.mirage-session.json).
pitfalls: INTENT IS SELF-REPORTED, NOT OBSERVED — never render it as solid ground truth. The system prompt only says the agent 'may show your reasoning wrapped in <thinking>' (server.py L820-822). When the agent skips the tags, steps.reasoning is empty: show 'No stated intent for this step', not a fabricated or LLM-summarized intent. The intent row must carry a muted 'self-reported · AG-UI THINKING' chip and reserve the solid 'observed' slot for a future cognition plane.

DO NOT correlate from the live useAgentStream reducer. Its VfsOp type drops tool_call_id/fingerprint/revision (agui.ts L160-168; reducer CUSTOM case L322-328 keeps only op/path/source/bytes/mount_prefix/duration_ms/timestamp). The intent≠effect flag, the diff fingerprint, and the 'dispatched from' join are all reliable only from the persisted /replay path. Build the card off /replay + getSessionTrace, treat the live stream as a tail-only preview.

is_cache is DERIVED (source=='ram', server.py L1702), and cache reads emit NO VfsOp action at all — so never invent a phantom 'cache hit' action in the list. Label the 'cache' chip muted. Likewise fingerprint/revision are real only on S3-like sources; on Fake*Resource(DiskResource) mounts they are null — render '—, S3-only via ETag', never a fake drift indicator.

SKIP-ACTION is a pure client-side re-fold what-if, NOT a re-execution. Banner it 'hypothetical: action N skipped' with one-click revert. Enable it only for recomputable state (overlay/reads); for anything backing-FS-dependent, disable with a tooltip — full-FS backing reconstruction is explicitly deferred (StatePage.tsx L262-264).

reads_so_far is a sorted SET OF PATHS only (server.py L1749) — it has no per-read bytes, ordering, or fingerprint. Don't draw a byte-accurate read timeline from it; for that granularity iterate actions[] read ops directly. The State tab's Reads node should say 'paths only'.

The cursor defaults to total-1 (last action, server.py L1775-1776), and idx is gap-free == OpRecord position. Don't assume idx maps to AG-UI seq or wall-clock order across BOTH streams; the firehose 'op' events are capped at last-20-per-command (DESIGN.md L88) while the persisted path is uncapped — if you ever merge firehose+replay, flag the discrepancy and prefer /replay.

The INTENT≠EFFECT flag must be conservative on the demo. There is no semantic NLP ground truth — it is a heuristic over self-reported text vs observed op (e.g. reasoning contains 'live/latest/current' but effect is is_cache=true; or reasoning names path A but the VfsOp read path B). Label it as a heuristic ('possible mismatch'), and never fire it when intent is absent (no intent = no claim to contradict).

Don't re-litigate the converged IA (DESIGN.md): no page-switcher, lenses-over-one-cursor, transport pinned bottom, governance demoted to quiet effect-class dots. The v3 additions (intent+command card, /replay-backed time-travel) extend the StepCard/ToolCallRow/ReasoningBlock + OverlayDiff primitives rather than replacing them — reuse, don't rebuild.
